status: Candidate development study; bounded literature search does not establish worldwide priority. No first-ever or submission-readiness claim is authorized by these pilot results.
candidate: Post-distillation, content-watermark task-vector filtering using a finite-horizon survival direction, with block-constant clean-gradient energy as a curvature proxy. Retains the existing extractor and architecture; normalizes to equal perturbation energy.
distinction_to_test: Unlike CTV redistillation and FSW internal-activation ownership verification, this candidate filters an already distilled content watermark for output-only owner verification. It is a specific algorithmic hypothesis, not a claim that curvature filtering or parameter stability is new.
mandatory_controls: paired generation seeds and content preservation
held-out clean-update attack data and optimizer
shuffled-curvature and utility-matched scaling controls before confirmatory claims

papers.title: PRO
papers.relationship: Jointly learns a text watermark policy and model, with a forgetting-perturbation regularizer. A generic adversarial-training defense is not new.

papers.title: FSW
papers.relationship: Uses a generalized eigenproblem and spectral truncation on intermediate representations; verification requires white-box representation access. Generic stable subspace watermarking is not new.

papers.title: CTV durability study
papers.relationship: Uses a contrastive task-vector Boolean parameter mask for targeted distillation. Selecting parameters resistant to clean training is not new.

papers.title: Merge-Adversarial Training
papers.relationship: Trains watermark distillation through simulated linear model merging. Generic merge-adversarial distillation is not new.

papers.title: RoboSignature: Robust Signature and Watermarking on Network Attacks
papers.relationship: Already applies tamper-resistant meta fine-tuning to Stable Signature image decoders, using attacked-model watermark/reconstruction loss and a retention loss. Generic MAML/TAR hardening for images is not new; no such method has been implemented as a new contribution here.

papers.title: DistSeal, published ICML2026 full29pageversion
papers.relationship: AppendixG already studies single-class clean LoRA forgetting;AppendixH studies composition with other watermarking schemes. Neither ordinary clean forgetting nor generic watermark stacking can be claimed as a new contribution.

papers.title: TextSeal full41pagev2
papers.relationship: Native methods, assumptions, repeated-context handling, calibration and limits checked against full text. This is prior art, not a new contribution.

papers.title: TextSeal2 full29pagev1
papers.relationship: Native methods, assumptions, repeated-context handling, calibration and limits checked against full text. This is prior art, not a new contribution.

papers.title: Meet Students Where They Are: Student-Prefix Teacher Adaptation for On-Policy Distillation
papers.relationship: Already adapts teachers to student prefixes with RLVR, then freezes them for standard OPD. Generic teacher adaptation, on-policy prefixes, or exposure-bias repair are not new. The watermark transport candidate concerns a marked target after clean parameter adaptation, not a claim to invent teacher adaptation.

papers.title: A Unified Attack Framework against Statistical Generative Watermarks for Large Language Models
papers.relationship: Read all35pages including proof appendices. Probability-ratio attacks are prior art and mandatory adaptive control for conditional exposure. Paper uses repeated sampled outputs; our proposed exposed-top10 ratio tilt is not a faithful replication of that estimator. General theorem statements require explicit score-alignment and fresh-key null-invariance, which are not established for TextSeal2. Perplexity alone does not establish content preservation.

papers.title: textGrain: Entropy-Calibrated Watermarking for Language Model Text
papers.relationship: Distinct entropy-budgeted block-OT watermark baseline. Any local reimplementation must check corrected marginals, achieved versus requested entropy loss, conditional selected-column probabilities, fresh-key assumptions and context-only deduplication. Support pruning is a separate API contract change, not unbiased watermark generation or an entropy guarantee.

papers.title: Watermark Smoothing Attacks against Language Models
papers.relationship: Prior smoothing attack uses top-K probabilities, confidence calibration and a reference-model mixture. AppendixD already proposes restricting confidence-related API information, including returning only the top token without probabilities. Generic probability hiding or support restriction is not new. The narrower candidate optimizes a keyed evidence floor under a retained-mass budget and leaves retained probabilities unchanged; priority still requires further comparison. Prior population fluency/diversity differs from source-preserving rewrites here.

papers.title: Scalable watermarking for identifying large language model outputs (SynthID-Text)
papers.relationship: Independent tournament watermark baseline. Main paper includes repeated-context masking and algorithm; default experiments useH4,m30,Bernoulli(.5),N2 and a learned Bayesian detector at empiricalFPR. A current official frequentist detector is a separately declared scoring choice. Conditional law must reflect post-temperature/top-p probabilities; masking and inter-response history must be explicit. Supplement-specific claims remain unverified.
